test_prompts.title: Modal Spectrum
test_prompts.concept: 같은 멜로디를 4개 모드(Dorian→Mixolydian→Phrygian→Lydian)로 지정 — 모드명이 실제 음계 차이를 만드는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: Dorian(3회), Mixolydian(2회), Phrygian(5회), Lydian(1회) — 코퍼스에 희소하게 존재
test_prompts.sp: Jazz piano trio exploring four different modes over the same root note D. Section A plays a melody in D Dorian mode, giving a minor quality with a raised sixth. Section B shifts to D Mixolydian mode, creating a major feel with a flatted seventh, bluesy and relaxed. Section C moves to D Phrygian mode, dark and Spanish-flavored with the characteristic half-step between the first and second notes. Section D brightens into D Lydian mode with a raised fourth creating a dreamy, floating quality. Upright bass walks underneath. Brushed drums keep a light swing. Each mode plays for 16 bars. 120 BPM. 4/4 time. Intimate jazz club recording.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Section A — D Dorian]
[piano melody, minor with raised sixth]
[upright bass walking]
[brushed drums, swing]
(modal jazz, cool and sophisticated)

[Section B — D Mixolydian]
[same melody shape, flatted seventh]
[bass adjusts to major feel]
(bluesy, relaxed, dominant quality)

[Section C — D Phrygian]
[same melody, half-step from root]
[bass darker pattern]
(Spanish, mysterious, tense)

[Section D — D Lydian]
[same melody, raised fourth]
[bass lighter walking]
(dreamy, floating, bright)

[Coda]
[piano returns to Dorian]
[single chord, letting ring]
(home)

test_prompts.title: Four Sevenths
test_prompts.concept: 7th 코드 4종(dominant 7th / major 7th / minor 7th / diminished 7th) — 같은 루트에서 7th 종류에 따른 색채 차이를 Suno가 구분하는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: seventh(21회) — 코퍼스에 존재하지만 세부 종류 구분은 0회
test_prompts.sp: Solo piano piece presenting four types of seventh chords on the root C. Section A features a dominant seventh chord with a bright, tense, unresolved sound that wants to move forward. Section B uses a major seventh chord, lush and warm, the sound of a romantic ballad. Section C plays a minor seventh chord, melancholic and introspective, cool jazz coloring. Section D introduces a diminished seventh chord, anxious and unstable, every note pulling in a different direction. Each section arpegiates the chord slowly, then plays a short melody using the chord tones. 72 BPM in free tempo. Close-miked grand piano. No reverb.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Section A — Dominant Seventh]
[piano C dominant seventh chord, arpeggiated]
[short melody using chord tones]
(tense, unresolved, leaning forward)

[Section B — Major Seventh]
[piano C major seventh chord, arpeggiated]
[same melodic shape, different color]
(lush, warm, romantic)

[Section C — Minor Seventh]
[piano C minor seventh chord, arpeggiated]
[melody now darker]
(cool, melancholic, jazz)

[Section D — Diminished Seventh]
[piano C diminished seventh, arpeggiated]
[melody anxious, unstable]
(tense, every note pulling away)

[Comparison]
[all four seventh chords played back to back]
[dominant, major, minor, diminished]
(hearing the difference)

[Final]
[C major seventh, sustained, fading]
(resolution into warmth)

test_prompts.concept: 구체적 코드명(Am7, Cmaj7, F#dim, Bb9)을 SP에 직접 투입 — 데드존(0회) 정면 도전

test_prompts.concept: 로마 숫자 코드 진행 표기(I-IV-V-I, ii-V-I, I-vi-IV-V)를 SP에 직접 투입 — 데드존(0회) 정면 도전
test_prompts.sp: Pop rock song demonstrating three classic chord progressions. The verse uses a I-IV-V-I progression in G major, the most fundamental harmonic movement in Western music. The pre-chorus shifts to a ii-V-I jazz turnaround, adding sophistication with the minor second chord leading to the dominant. The chorus uses I-vi-IV-V, the iconic four-chord progression heard in countless pop songs. Electric guitar plays power chords in the verse, clean arpeggios in the pre-chorus, and full strumming in the chorus. Bass guitar follows the root movement. Drums build from verse to chorus. 110 BPM in G major. 4/4 time. Rock studio production.

[electric guitar power chords]

test_prompts.title: Chromatic Tension Lab
test_prompts.concept: 화성학 중급 용어(chromatic passing tone, tritone substitution, secondary dominant) — 경계선 탐색
test_prompts.sp: Jazz combo piece exploring chromatic harmony techniques. The piano plays a standard jazz progression but introduces chromatic passing tones between each chord change, creating smooth voice leading with half-step connections. A tritone substitution replaces the dominant V chord with a chord a tritone away, creating a surprising chromatic bass descent. A secondary dominant chord temporarily tonicizes the IV chord, briefly making it sound like a new key center. The bass plays chromatic walking lines connecting chord tones. Guitar comps with altered dominant chords using sharp-nine and flat-thirteen extensions. Drums play a medium swing pattern. 130 BPM in C major. 4/4 time with swing feel. Live studio session.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Head — Standard Changes]
[piano standard jazz chords]
[bass walking, diatonic]
[drums medium swing]
(the foundation, clean and clear)

[Chromatic Passing Tones]
[piano half-step connections between chords]
[bass chromatic walking line]
(smooth, slippery, sliding between)

[Tritone Substitution]
[piano replaces V with bII]
[bass descending chromatically]
(surprise — the expected chord replaced)

[Secondary Dominant]
[V of IV — briefly a new key center]
[bass and piano pivot together]
(a detour that makes the destination sweeter)

[Altered Dominants]
[guitar sharp-nine, flat-thirteen voicings]
[piano clashing but beautiful]
(tension pushed to the edge)

[Resolution]
[back to simple I chord, no extensions]
[bass on the root]
(home after the journey)

test_prompts.title: The Pedal Point
test_prompts.concept: 페달 포인트(pedal point on tonic, dominant pedal) — 코퍼스에 존재하는 화성 개념(4회)의 확장
test_prompts.sp: Ambient rock piece built on pedal point harmony. The bass guitar holds a single low E note throughout the entire piece as a tonic pedal point, never changing. Above this pedal, the guitar plays chords that move freely: E minor, C major, A minor, D major, G major — all heard against the unchanging E bass. The effect is a constantly shifting harmonic color over a stable foundation. In the bridge, the pedal shifts to B, creating a dominant pedal that generates tension wanting to resolve back to E. The synth pad provides sustained harmonic clouds. Drums play a spacious pattern with lots of cymbal wash. 90 BPM in E minor. 4/4 time. Spacious reverb.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Intro — Tonic Pedal]
[bass guitar, single low E, sustained]
[guitar E minor chord above]
[drums spacious]
(the foundation that never moves)

[Verse — Chords Over Pedal]
[bass still on E]
[guitar: C major over E pedal]
[guitar: A minor over E pedal]
(the chords change but the earth stays)

[Chorus — More Movement]
[bass still on E]
[guitar: D major over E — tension]
[guitar: G major over E — brightness]
[synth pad harmonic cloud]
(colors shifting above the anchor)

[Bridge — Dominant Pedal]
[bass shifts to B — dominant pedal]
[guitar chords above B]
(tension, wanting to go home)

[Resolution]
[bass returns to E]
[guitar simple E minor]
(the pedal returns, relief)

[Outro]
[bass E, fading]
[guitar harmonic]
(the last vibration)

test_prompts.title: Scale Colors
test_prompts.concept: 스케일 종류별 음향(minor pentatonic / blues scale / whole tone / octatonic) — 스케일명의 해상도
test_prompts.corpus_reference: pentatonic(9회), blues scale(2회), whole tone(0회), octatonic(0회)
test_prompts.sp: Electric guitar solo piece exploring four different scales over a static chord vamp. Section A uses the minor pentatonic scale, the backbone of blues and rock soloing, with five notes creating a raw, soulful sound. Section B adds the blue note to create a blues scale, adding a gritty, expressive passing tone between the fourth and fifth. Section C uses a whole tone scale where every interval is a whole step, creating a dreamlike, floating quality with no sense of resolution. Section D uses an octatonic scale alternating whole and half steps, creating a symmetrical, disorienting, Stravinsky-like sound. Backing: a single power chord vamp on E with bass and drums. 100 BPM. 4/4 time. Dry, direct guitar tone.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Section A — Minor Pentatonic]
[guitar solo, five-note scale]
[bass and drums E power chord vamp]
(raw, soulful, the blues DNA)

[Section B — Blues Scale]
[guitar adding the blue note]
[same backing vamp]
(grittier, more expressive, the extra spice)

[Section C — Whole Tone Scale]
[guitar all whole steps, no half steps]
[bass shifts to whole tone bass line]
(dreamlike, floating, no gravity)

[Section D — Octatonic Scale]
[guitar alternating whole-half steps]
[bass chromatic movement]
(disorienting, symmetrical, Stravinsky)

[Comparison]
[four-bar phrase in each scale, back to back]
(pentatonic → blues → whole tone → octatonic)

[Ending]
[guitar returns to pentatonic]
[single bent note, fading]
(home is five notes)

test_prompts.title: Cadence Catalog
test_prompts.concept: 카덴스 유형(perfect / plagal / deceptive / half cadence) — 코퍼스에 있는 plagal(7회)에서 출발하여 확장
test_prompts.sp: Piano and string quartet piece demonstrating four types of musical cadence. Section A ends with a perfect cadence, the strongest resolution — the dominant chord moving to the tonic like a period at the end of a sentence. Section B ends with a plagal cadence, the gentle resolution — the subdominant moving to the tonic, the 'amen' cadence heard in hymns. Section C ends with a deceptive cadence — the dominant chord that should resolve to the tonic instead moves to the submediant, a surprise that delays resolution. Section D ends with a half cadence, stopping on the dominant chord, an incomplete sentence that leaves the listener hanging. Each section plays the same eight-bar melody but with a different ending. Piano and string quartet. 80 BPM in C major. 4/4 time. Concert hall reverb.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Section A — Perfect Cadence]
[piano and strings, eight-bar melody]
[ending: V to I — complete resolution]
(a sentence with a period)

[Section B — Plagal Cadence]
[same melody]
[ending: IV to I — gentle amen]
(a prayer ending softly)

[Section C — Deceptive Cadence]
[same melody]
[ending: V to vi — surprise, not home]
(the door you expected is the wrong one)

[Section D — Half Cadence]
[same melody]
[ending: stops on V — hanging, unfinished]
(a sentence without a period)

[Comparison]
[same four-bar phrase, four endings back to back]
[perfect, plagal, deceptive, half]
(four ways to end — or not end)

[Final]
[piano alone, perfect cadence, V to I]
[strings sustain the tonic]
(the only true ending)

test_prompts.title: The Key Change
test_prompts.concept: 구체적 전조 지시(C major → E-flat major) — key change(1회)가 데드존 근처, 전조의 구체적 목표 키 지정이 먹히는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: key change(1회), modulation(0회), key of X(652회)
test_prompts.sp: Pop anthem that modulates through three keys for emotional escalation. The song starts in C major with a straightforward verse and chorus. At the second chorus, the key modulates up to D major, a whole step higher, creating a lift in energy and brightness. The final chorus modulates up again to E-flat major, another half step, the classic truck driver modulation that pushes the emotional climax to its peak. Each modulation is preceded by a two-bar transition using the dominant of the new key. Piano, electric guitar, bass, and drums. Male vocal in a pop rock style. 118 BPM. 4/4 time. Big pop production with wide stereo.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Verse 1 — C major]
[piano and guitar, C major]
[male vocal, comfortable range]
Every road I've ever known
Led me back to where I've grown
But tonight I'm breaking through
Finding something brave and new

[Chorus 1 — C major]
[full band, C major]
Rise, rise, higher than before
Rise, rise, there's always something more

[Verse 2 — still C major]
[same arrangement]
Every wall I've ever built
Crumbles underneath my guilt
But the sky is wide and clear
And I'm done with living here

[Modulation — C to D major]
[two-bar transition, dominant of D]
(the lift, the key is rising)

[Chorus 2 — D major]
[full band, D major — brighter, higher]
Rise, rise, higher than before
Rise, rise, there's always something more

[Modulation — D to E-flat major]
[two-bar transition, dominant of E-flat]
(one more push, the final climb)

[Final Chorus — E-flat major]
[full band, E-flat major — peak energy]
Rise, rise, higher than before
Rise, rise, there's always something more
(the truck driver modulation — maximum emotion)

[Outro — E-flat major]
[guitar and piano fading]
[vocal ad lib, high]
(staying in the new key, never going back)
